chain.label: Operator's maintenance records incomplete and unavailable
chain.trigger: no maintenance logbooks from April 1999 to the time of the accident were provided to the Board

chain.label: Unresolved repeat right engine flameouts
chain.trigger: the right engine flamed out again... the cause of the flameout once again could not be determined

caused_by.evidence: Because Pavair did not provide the inspector with the accident airplane's maintenance records, he placed an aircraft condition notice on the airplane

chain.label: FSDO verbally released airplane without receiving required records
chain.trigger: he verbally released the airplane for operations... Pavair's maintenance records for the accident airplane were never received by the Riverside FSDO

caused_by.evidence: JETT reported (on behalf of Pavair) that it had complied with the limitations of the condition notice

chain.label: Incomplete Learjet 24 recurrent training and very low-time first officer
chain.trigger: the captain began recurrent Learjet 24 training at AAN but did not complete the training... [the first officer] had accumulated 250 total flight hours

chain.label: Undetermined in-flight problem during climb prompting return request
chain.trigger: as the airplane was climbing through an altitude of 26,000 feet, the first officer requested a return to CNO

caused_by.evidence: the accident airplane's right engine flamed out... the cause of the flameout could not be determined
he verbally released the airplane for operations

chain.label: Airplane descended through assigned altitude at rapidly increasing rate
chain.trigger: Radar data showed the airplane descending through 23,000 feet at a rate of about 6,500 fpm... The first officer did not respond.

caused_by.evidence: about 2.5 minutes had elapsed from the flight crew's request to return to the departure airport and the declaration of the emergency

chain.label: Departure from controlled flight into near-vertical descent
chain.trigger: departed controlled flight, entered a near-vertical descent... he observed the airplane's nose pitch 'straight down'

caused_by.evidence: The descent rate then rapidly increased to 6,500 fpm and then to 10,000 fpm
the first officer received Learjet 20 series differences training so that he could fly those airplanes as second-in-command to build his flight time experience

chain.label: Impact with high desert terrain and destruction of airplane
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted high desert terrain (an elevation of 3,350 feet) about 3 miles southeast of Helendale

caused_by.evidence: the airplane remained in a nose-down attitude until it impacted terrain and exploded

chain.label: Both pilots fatally injured
chain.trigger: The captain and the first officer were killed... the cause of death for the pilots was massive blunt force trauma

caused_by.evidence: the airplane exploded into a 'mushroom cloud' when it impacted terrain
